cohort: The study included 120 ASA I-II parturients aged 20-35 years undergoing elective lower segment caesarean section (LSCS).
finding: Baseline Perfusion Index is a reliable predictor of post-spinal hypotension in LSCS, and phenylephrine is more effective than ephedrine for hemodynamic stabilization in these cases.
mod_finding: The study found that Baseline Perfusion Index is a reliable predictor of post-spinal hypotension in parturients undergoing LSCS, and phenylephrine demonstrates superior efficacy over ephedrine for hemodynamic stabilization during LSCS.
